comment: The ref kinds and EVENTS this factory declares BEYOND the instrument's core set. Core ref kinds are row, subject, commit, session, rework; core events are genesis, intake, claim, dispatch, close, score, ruling, run. A declaration ADDS; it never removes or redefines a core entry. DECLARED HERE: 'issue'. Reason, measured 2026-09-29: a CAMPAIGN unit's subject is a descriptive stem (campaign-<what-it-does>) by this factory's storage law, because the ledger's bare `#N` subject namespace belongs to the CANONICAL SERVICE board (alexeyleshchenko/ai-antispam), and the campaign board (leshchenko1979/ai-antispam-outreach) numbers independently. So a campaign unit had NO lawful way to point at its own board issue: `subject` cannot carry a bare number without colliding with the service namespace, and the core kinds hold no object of that shape. The kind was forced by row n=118 (the #23 claim), which carried `issue:23` -- accepted silently at append and flagged only by `verify`, one step later (see the write-path gap reported alongside this declaration). VALUE: an issue NUMBER on the board that owns the subject's work -- campaign board for a campaign-* subject. This adds a pointer, never a lifecycle: an `issue` ref does not discharge intake/claim/close, which remain the subject's legs.
